title: 第145章 夏末第144章 族会
content_zh:
夏天快要过完的时候，杏树上的果子终于全熟了。黄的，软的，挂在枝条上，像是被阳光烤透了的铃铛，风一吹就轻轻晃动。方小石那天下下午跑来了，站在院门口，还没进门就喊：“方圆哥，杏子熟了没？”方圆从屋里走出来，看了一眼那棵杏树，“熟了。”方小石跑过去，站在树前面看了看，又抬头看了一圈，挑了一颗最黄的，轻轻一拧就摘了下来，放进嘴里咬了一口。嚼了两下，他的眼睛就亮了。“好甜！”方圆站在他身后，没有说让他慢点吃，也没有说别吃太多。方小石站在树前面，一连吃了好几颗，直到嘴巴塞满了才停下来，含糊不清地说：“方圆哥，这棵树明年还能结更多吧？”“能。只要它还活着。”方小石点了点头，像是记住了这个答案。他又摘了几颗，用衣摆兜住，说带回去给他娘尝尝，然后跑走了，脚步声在巷子里越来越远。
方小石走了之后，方圆也摘了几颗杏，放在石桌上。王紫璇从厨房出来，拿了一颗，咬了一口，“比去年我娘家的杏甜。”“因为是你种的。”王紫璇没有接话，又咬了一口，嚼了很久才咽下去。她低头看着手里那颗被咬了一半的杏，像是在想什么，又像是什么都没想，只是借着这一口甜，把什么话也一并咽了下去。
下午的时候，楚云飞来了。他穿着一件灰色的短衫，像是赶了远路，进了院子之后没有坐下，先走到那棵杏树前面看了看。“这树是你种的？”“王紫璇种的。”“结得不错。”楚云飞摘了一颗，咬了一口，“甜。比中州城的杏甜。”方圆在石凳上坐下，“你怎么来了？”“路过。想去南边看看，走到青州，就拐进来看看你。”楚云飞在他对面坐下，打量了一下院子，“你这里比上次来的时候更满了。”方圆顺着他的目光看了一圈——枣树、杏树、小枣树，三棵树已经把墙角那块地方撑满了。风吹过的时候，三棵树的叶子叠在一起，像是在悄悄交换什么消息。他说：“是满了。”
楚云飞没有多留，喝了一碗茶，吃了几颗杏，就站起来，“我走了。天黑之前要赶到下一个镇子。”方圆送他到门口。“你以后还走吗？”“走。走到走不动为止。”楚云飞回头看了他一眼，“你就打算一直待在这里了？”“待在这里。”“也好。”楚云飞转身走了。他的背影在巷子里越走越远，和方小石的背影不一样——方小石是跑着走的，他是走着走的，一步一步的，不紧不慢，像是已经习惯了这种一个人的路。方圆站在门口，看着他的背影消失，然后关上门，回到院子里。
傍晚的时候，方圆坐在石桌旁，手里拿着一颗杏，没有吃。王紫璇从厨房出来，在他旁边坐下。“楚云飞走了？”“走了。”“他说什么了？”“说他还要继续走。”“你不问他去哪里？”“问了。他说走到走不动为止。”王紫璇没有再问，只是也拿起一颗杏，握在手心，没有吃，像是在替某个人感受这一整个夏天的重量。她在夏末的风里捏了捏那颗杏，又把它放回桌上，像是帮一个路过的朋友确认过了，这棵树的果子确实够甜。
夏天的最后一天，青州城下了一场小雨。雨不大，细细的，落在院子里的青石板上。槐树的叶子被雨洗过之后更绿了。方圆坐在正房门口，看着雨落下来，院墙外的巷子里隐约传来晚归的人收起晾衣竿的声响，一路响过去，很快就静了。他想起楚云飞走的时候说“走到走不动为止”——有些人一辈子都在路上，有些人走了一阵就停下来了。他停下来，不是因为他走不动了，是因为他找到了想停下来的地方。雨滴答滴答地落在瓦片上，像是有人拿一把小锤子，在屋顶上敲着很慢的节奏。
王紫璇端着两碗绿豆汤从厨房出来，一碗递给他，一碗自己端着。她在旁边的门槛上坐下来，屋檐刚好挡住雨，雨水从瓦缝里落下来，在他们面前挂起一道透明的帘子。“明天就立秋了。”“嗯。”“夏天过完了。”“嗯。”“今年夏天，你觉得长不长？”“长。”王紫璇低头喝了一口绿豆汤，“我觉得短。”
雨停的时候，天已经全黑了。方圆把空碗收进厨房，出来的时候，看到王紫璇还坐在门槛上，没有走。她坐在那里，看着院子里的树，像是在跟这个夏天做最后的道别。他在她旁边坐下。“你还不回去？”“再坐一会儿。”两人坐在门槛上，看着院子里的树影。月亮从云层后面钻出来，照在湿漉漉的青石板上，也照亮了那三棵树。它们站在那里，像是已经商量好了明年怎么长。方圆不知道明年会不会比今年更好，但他知道，它们还会站在那里。
第二天早上，方圆醒来的时候，天已经凉了一些。他走到院子里，空气里带着秋天的味道——干爽的，凉丝丝的，没有了夏天的闷热。他站在枣树前面，看到枝条上的枣子已经开始泛红了，一颗一颗的，像小灯笼挂在上面。他伸手碰了一下其中一颗，硬硬的，还没有完全熟。但他不急。枣子会自己熟，秋天会慢慢来，日子也会一天一天地过。他转身走进厨房，生火煮粥。粥滚了，水面冒起细密的气泡，他把火调小，盖上盖子，又走到院子里蹲下来，伸手碰了碰那棵小枣树的叶子，像秋天在跟它打招呼，又像冬天在提前替它盖好被子。他站起来，拍了拍手上的土，转身走回厨房。粥刚好煮好，他盛了两碗，端到石桌上。太阳升起来了，照着院子里的树，照着石桌上的粥碗，照着那个正推门进来的身影。他坐下来，端起粥碗，喝了一口。粥很烫，但他没有放下。
：8xiaoshuo。：wap.8xiaoshuo
content_en:
When summer is coming to an end, the fruits on the apricot trees are finally fully ripe. Yellow and soft, hanging on the branches, like bells baked by the sun, swaying gently when the wind blows. Fang Xiaoshi ran over that afternoon and stood at the door of the courtyard. Before he entered, he called out: "Brother Fangyuan, are the apricots ripe?" Fangyuan walked out of the house and took a look at the apricot tree. "They are ripe." Fang Xiaoshi ran over, stood in front of the tree and looked at it. He looked around again, picked the yellowest one, picked it off with a twist, put it in his mouth and took a bite. After chewing it twice, his eyes lit up. "So sweet!" Fang Yuan stood behind him, not telling him to eat slowly or not to eat too much. Fang Xiaoshi stood in front of the tree and ate several in a row. He didn't stop until his mouth was full, and said vaguely: "Brother Fangyuan, can this tree bear more fruits next year?" "Yes. As long as it is alive." Fang Xiaoshi nodded, as if he had memorized the answer. He picked a few more, pocketed them with the hem of his clothes, and said he would take them back to his mother to taste. Then he ran away, his footsteps getting farther and farther in the alley.
After Fang Xiaoshi left, Fangyuan also picked a few apricots and placed them on the stone table. Wang Zixuan came out of the kitchen, took one, and took a bite. "It's sweeter than my parents' apricot last year." "Because you grew it." Wang Zixuan didn't answer, took another bite, and chewed it for a long time before swallowing it. She looked down at the half-bitten apricot in her hand, as if she was thinking about something, but also as if she was not thinking about anything at all. She just swallowed all the words with this sweet bite.
In the afternoon, Chu Yunfei came. He was wearing a gray short shirt, as if he had traveled a long way. After entering the yard, he did not sit down. He first walked to the almond tree and took a look. "Did you plant this tree?" "Wang Zixuan planted it." "It bears well." Chu Yunfei picked one and took a bite, "Sweet. Sweeter than the apricots in Zhongzhou City." Fang Yuan sat down on the stone bench, "Why are you here?" "Passing by. I want to go to the south and go to Qingzhou. Just turn in and see you." Chu Yunfei sat down opposite him and looked around the yard, "Your place is fuller than the last time I came here." Fang Yuan followed his gaze and looked around - the jujube tree, the apricot tree, and the small jujube tree, the three trees had already filled the corner. When the wind blows, the leaves of the three trees overlap each other, as if they are secretly exchanging some news. He said, "It's full."
Chu Yunfei didn't stay long. He drank a bowl of tea and ate a few apricots, then stood up and said, "I'm leaving. I have to get to the next town before dark." Fangyuan walked him to the door. "Are you going to leave in the future?" "Go. Until you can't walk anymore." Chu Yunfei looked back at him and said, "Are you going to stay here forever?" "Stay here." "That's fine." Chu Yunfei turned and walked away. His back walked farther and farther in the alley, which was different from Fang Xiaoshi's back - Fang Xiaoshi was running, and he was walking, step by step, unhurriedly, as if he was used to this kind of road alone. Fangyuan stood at the door, watching his back disappear, then closed the door and returned to the yard.
In the evening, Fang Yuan sat at the stone table, holding an apricot in his hand but not eating it. Wang Zixuan came out of the kitchen and sat down next to him. "Chu Yunfei left?" "He left." "What did he say?" "Said he was going to keep walking." "You didn't ask him where he was going?" "Asked. He said he would go until he couldn't walk anymore." Wang Zixuan didn't ask any more questions, but just picked up an apricot and held it in the palm of her hand without eating it, as if she was feeling the weight of the entire summer for someone. She pinched the apricot in the late summer wind and put it back on the table, as if confirming for a passing friend that the fruit of this tree was indeed sweet enough.
On the last day of summer, it rained lightly in Qingzhou City. The rain was not heavy, falling lightly on the bluestone in the yard. The leaves of the locust tree are greener after being washed by the rain. Fangyuan is sitting at the door of the main roomMouth, watching the rain fall, the faint sound of people returning late putting away the clothes drying pole could be heard in the alley outside the courtyard wall. It sounded all the way, and soon became quiet. He remembered that when Chu Yunfei left, he said "until you can't walk anymore" - some people stay on the road all their lives, and some people stop after walking for a while. He stopped, not because he couldn't walk anymore, but because he found the place where he wanted to stop. The raindrops fell on the tiles, as if someone was tapping a small hammer on the roof in a slow rhythm.
Wang Zixuan came out of the kitchen with two bowls of mung bean soup, handing one bowl to him and holding the other herself. She sat down on the threshold next to her. The eaves just blocked the rain. The rainwater fell from the cracks in the tiles, and a transparent curtain was hung in front of them. "Tomorrow will be the beginning of autumn." "Yes." "Summer is over." "Yes." "Do you think this summer will be long?" "Long." Wang Zixuan lowered her head and took a sip of mung bean soup, "I think it will be short."
When the rain stopped, it was completely dark. Fangyuan put the empty bowl into the kitchen. When he came out, he saw Wang Zixuan still sitting on the threshold and not leaving. She sat there, looking at the trees in the yard, as if saying her last goodbyes to this summer. He sat down next to her. "Aren't you going back?" "Sit a little longer." The two of them sat on the threshold and looked at the shadows of the trees in the yard. The moon emerged from behind the clouds, shining on the wet bluestone and also illuminating the three trees. They stood there as if they had already decided how they would grow next year. Fangyuan didn't know if next year would be better than this year, but he knew they would still be there.
The next morning, when Fangyuan woke up, it was already cooler. He walked to the yard, and the air carried the smell of autumn - dry and cool, without the sultry heat of summer. He stood in front of the date tree and saw that the dates on the branches had begun to turn red, one by one, like small lanterns hanging on it. He reached out and touched one of them. It was hard and not yet fully cooked. But he's in no hurry. The dates will ripen on their own, autumn will come slowly, and the days will pass day by day. He turned around and walked into the kitchen, lighting the fire and making porridge. The porridge was rolling, and fine bubbles appeared on the water. He turned down the heat, closed the lid, walked to the yard and squatted down, reaching out and touching the leaves of the little jujube tree, as if he was greeting it in autumn, and like he was covering it with a quilt in advance in winter. He stood up, patted the dirt on his hands, turned around and walked back to the kitchen. The porridge was just ready, so he filled two bowls and brought them to the stone table. The sun has risen, shining on the trees in the yard, the porridge bowl on the stone table, and the figure who is pushing the door in. He sat down, picked up the porridge bowl, and took a sip. The porridge was very hot, but he didn't put it down.
